ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are two separate chemical structures in the figure, and they have curved arrows; the question requires ignoring the arrows. The lower-left structure is labeled H3C–OH, and is a molecule in which a methyl group is connected to a hydroxyl group. The upper-right structure shows O=C=N–S, where S also forms double bonds with two oxygen atoms and forms a single bond with Cl. Then reason: After ignoring all curved arrows, only record covalent connections. The lower-left H3C–OH corresponds to methanol, with SMILES as CO. The upper-right molecule is O=C=N–S(=O)(=O)Cl, corresponding to SMILES as O=C=NS(=O)(=O)Cl. The two structures are separated from each other in the figure, so connect the two SMILES with a dot.

method.method_draft: First inspect the drawing and list only the covalent atoms/bonds, excluding curved arrows. Transcribe the lower-left molecule H3C–OH as methanol, SMILES CO. Then transcribe the upper-right reagent as O=C=N attached to S, where S has two =O substituents and one Cl substituent, giving O=C=NS(=O)(=O)Cl. Since the two species are separate in the image, join their SMILES with a dot to obtain CO.O=C=NS(=O)(=O)Cl.
